From 2845989f2ebaf7848e4eccf9a779daf3156ea0a5 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Puranjay Mohan <puranjay@kernel.org>
Date: Fri, 17 Apr 2026 08:21:33 -0700
Subject: [PATCH] bpf: Validate node_id in arena_alloc_pages()

arena_alloc_pages() accepts a plain int node_id and forwards it through
the entire allocation chain without any bounds checking.

Validate node_id before passing it down the allocation chain in
arena_alloc_pages().

Fixes: 317460317a02 ("bpf: Introduce bpf_arena.")
Signed-off-by: Puranjay Mohan <puranjay@kernel.org>
Reviewed-by: Emil Tsalapatis <emil@etsalapatis.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20260417152135.1383754-1-puranjay@kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Alexei Starovoitov <ast@kernel.org>

diff --git a/kernel/bpf/arena.c b/kernel/bpf/arena.c
index 9c68c9b0b24a..523c3a61063b 100644
--- a/kernel/bpf/arena.c
+++ b/kernel/bpf/arena.c
@@ -562,6 +562,10 @@ static long arena_alloc_pages(struct bpf_arena *arena, long uaddr, long page_cnt
 	u32 uaddr32;
 	int ret, i;
 
+	if (node_id != NUMA_NO_NODE &&
+	    ((unsigned int)node_id >= nr_node_ids || !node_online(node_id)))
+		return 0;
+
 	if (page_cnt > page_cnt_max)
 		return 0;
 
-- 
2.34.1

The patch introduces a validation check for the `node_id` parameter in the `arena_alloc_pages()` function within `kernel/bpf/arena.c`. Previously, `node_id` was passed unchecked into the memory allocation chain, which could lead to invalid node references. The added check ensures that if `node_id` is not `NUMA_NO_NODE`, it must be a valid online node (i.e., less than `nr_node_ids` and actually online). If the check fails, the function returns 0, aborting the allocation. This prevents undefined behavior or errors caused by passing an out-of-bounds or offline node ID.

Since the modification is confined to a single file, there are no cross-file relationships to describe.

You are a programming expert.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
<text>
static long arena_alloc_pages(struct bpf_arena *arena, long uaddr, long page_cnt, int node_id, bool sleepable)
</text>
<text>
ret = bpf_map_alloc_pages(&arena->map, node_id, this_batch, pages);
</text>
Reason:
The function accepts a plain int `node_id` without any bounds or online checking and passes it directly to `bpf_map_alloc_pages()`, which forwards it to the memory allocation chain. An invalid node ID (e.g., negative, out of range, or offline) can lead to undefined behavior, memory corruption, or system errors.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
<text>
if (node_id != NUMA_NO_NODE &&
    ((unsigned int)node_id >= nr_node_ids || !node_online(node_id)))
    return 0;
</text>
Reason:
This validation ensures that if `node_id` is not `NUMA_NO_NODE`, it must be within the valid range (0 to `nr_node_ids-1`) and correspond to an online node. If the node ID is invalid, the function returns 0 (failure) early, preventing the invalid ID from being used in any subsequent memory allocation.
